subject: Data_00
note: Reviewed three sampled slices in each of three directions: tissue distributions and MNI/AAL alignment show no obvious global displacement. Local cortical and sulcal boundaries remain automatic segmentation estimates.

subject: Data_01
note: Reviewed three sampled slices in each of three directions: the brain and atlas are broadly aligned. Small residual tissues at the skull base after BET persist into tissue segmentation; local skull-base labels and boundaries require attention.

subject: Data_15
note: Reviewed three sampled slices in each of three directions: the brain, GM/WM distribution and nonlinear template/AAL are broadly aligned. Local boundaries at the frontal and temporal bases still require routine attention.

subject: Data_18
note: Reviewed three sampled slices in each of three directions: the brain and atlas are broadly aligned. Local registration differences remain around the ventricles and cortical folds; small skull-base remnants persist into tissue segmentation.

subject: Data_33
note: Reviewed three sampled slices in each of three directions: nonlinear registration follows the brain more closely than affine registration, and AAL shows no obvious global displacement. Source-image blur and local peripheral remnants leave uncertainty at cortical boundaries.

subject: Data_35
note: Reviewed three sampled slices in each of three directions: the brain and nonlinear template/AAL are broadly aligned. Source-image blur and irregular local frontal/cortical boundaries require continued quality notes for tissue classification and regional boundaries.

subject: Data_36
note: Reviewed three sampled slices in each of three directions: tissue distributions and nonlinear template/AAL are broadly aligned with the brain. Nonlinear registration improves affine-stage differences at frontal and temporal-base boundaries; local cortical-fold differences remain.

subject: Data_40
note: Reviewed three sampled slices in each of three directions: the brain and nonlinear template/AAL are broadly aligned. Small remnants at the lower brainstem/skull base and small tissue-classification speckles require attention.

subject: Data_44
note: Reviewed three sampled slices in each of three directions: the nonlinear template/AAL fits the brain and ventricles better than the affine result. Incomplete upper-frontal BET boundaries, peripheral remnants and local registration differences around enlarged ventricles remain visible. These limitations are retained in the current data.

subject: Data_49
note: Reviewed three sampled slices in each of three directions: tissue segmentation and nonlinear template/AAL are broadly aligned with the brain. Small classification speckles at the brainstem/skull base and local boundary differences require attention.
